slides.t: Hens need water every day, even in the cold. Frozen water means less drinking, and fewer eggs.
An insulated waterer holds warmth longer, so water freezes more slowly. It buys time, not a guarantee.
In hard freezes, add a heated base or swap in fresh water once or twice a day.
Enough capacity for your flock, easy filling and cleaning, and nipples or cups that resist icing up.
Indoor extension cords, heaters near dry bedding, skipped cleaning. Use outdoor-rated gear and check it daily.

hook: A gift for the gardener who has everything

slides.t: Usually a trowel, transplanter, cultivator and weeder. Small tools for planting, digging and weeding beds.
Trowel digs holes, transplanter has depth marks for bulbs, cultivator loosens soil, weeder pulls taproots.
Heads firmly fixed to the handle, steel that will not bend in clay, and grips that fit the hand.
A tote keeps tools together, so they do not get lost in the grass or left out in the rain.
Knock off soil, dry the tools, and wipe the metal with a little oil before winter storage.
